scenario: Constructed: acute vs chronic, single vs multiple, attenuation, invasion, a variant vs a neoplasm, clot burden, diffuse pneumonia distribution and descriptors, a benign-lesion size
description: Constructed. Acute vs chronic emboli is a major diagnosis error (the age); a solitary vs multiple nodules and abutment vs invasion are major extent errors (the side is scored upstream); ground-glass vs solid attenuation is a major character error; a small vs large clot burden is a major severity error. Residual thymus (a normal variant) vs a suspected thymoma is a status inversion scored upstream: no Stage 3b error. A mild vs moderate grade of emphysema is minor; a vessel list that leaves out the per-vessel grades is a major severity error. For a diffuse viral pneumonia, a coarser distribution is a minor site error and septal thickening vs consolidation within the ground glass a minor character error; a size difference on a chest wall lipoma (benign, not followed by its size) is a minor measurement error.

errors.reasoning: acute vs chronic segmental emboli; acute emboli call for anticoagulation now
solitary vs multiple nodules; primary vs metastatic workup
ground-glass vs solid 8 mm nodule; switches the Fleischner pathway
abutment vs invasion of the mediastinum; changes the T stage and resectability
large vs small clot burden, two steps; changes risk stratification and treatment
moderate vs mild emphysema; one step, same management
pred leaves out the mild LAD and RCA calcium grades gt gives; the grade sets the cardiovascular risk
both lungs vs peripheral lower-lobe ground glass; a coarser distribution of a diffuse pneumonia, same treatment
septal thickening vs consolidation within the ground glass; two descriptors of one diffuse pneumonia, same treatment
4.2 vs 3.0 cm chest wall lipoma, over 20 %; a lipoma is benign and not followed by its size
